papers.title_en: Controlling Variability in~Neuroimaging Analysis Pipelines with~Software Product Lines
papers.authors: Gauthier Le Bartz Lyan, Paul Temple, Boris Clenet, Mathieu Acher
papers.tldr: 神经影像分析中，MRI数据复杂且噪声大，不同团队针对同一问题搭建的分析流水线会产生显著结果差异，NARPS研究已揭示这一可重复性挑战。本文提出以软件产品线（SPL）原则组织这些功能相同但实现各异的流水线，并将从现有流水线反向工程出SPL视为关键难点。作者主张概念性采纳SPL以控制变异性，从而提升神经影像研究的可重复性与一致性。
papers.abstract_en: Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is an acquisition technique used for medical diagnosis. It is notably used for structural and functional MRI (or fMRI) image analysis. MRI data is known to be complex and noisy, so pipelines are created to extract and enhance relevant information in retrieved images. The NARPS study highlighted the significant variability that can emerge from different pipelines set up by independent teams while trying to answer the same research question about brain functioning. Having different implementations realizing the same task is a typical playground for software product lines (SPLs), which may be out of the sight of neuroimage practitioners. Thus, proposing an SPL out of these different pipelines falls back on a typical reverse-engineering problem with its usual difficulties. In this document, we advocate for the conceptual adoption of SPL principles as a promising direction to improve reproducibility and consistency in neuroimaging research.

papers.title_en: Phase-based Edge Coupling: Modeling Overlapping Functional Architectures and High-Order Edge-to-Edge Interactions in EEG Networks
papers.authors: Chengcheng Wu, Zichen Shi, Jiayang Xu, Shanbao Tong, Xiaoli Guo
papers.evidence: EEG脑网络的边中心功能耦合建模
papers.tldr: 传统EEG网络分析以节点为中心，难以刻画重叠功能架构与高阶边间交互。本文提出基于相位的边中心耦合算法PEC，用瞬时相位差构建边时间序列并以归一化内积量化边间耦合。仿真显示其耦合估计误差低于10%、抗虚假耦合AUROC超过0.7，并在个体与认知状态识别上优于PNC。该工作为EEG网络提供了可建模重叠模块和跨脑协调的新工具。
papers.abstract_en: Network neuroscience has traditionally relied on node-centric approaches, which are inherently limited in capturing the brain's overlapping functional architectures and higher-order edge-to-edge interactions. The emerging edge-centric paradigm addresses this gap by shifting the analytical unit from nodes to edges. However, while edge-centric models have been established for DTI and fMRI, comparable EEG methodologies have yet to be developed. In this study, we proposed a Phase-based Edge-centric Coupling (PEC) algorithm for EEG network modelling, where edge time series are derived from instantaneous phase differences of EEG signals and edge-to-edge coupling is quantified via normalized inner product. Simulation tests demonstrated the robustness of PEC algorithm, achieving high accuracy (<10% relative error) in coupling estimation and discriminative capacity (AUROC>0.7) against spurious coupling.When provided sufficient data length(>=16 cycles), PEC outperformed traditional Phase Node-centric Coupling (PNC) in both individual identifiability and cognitive-state identifiability, enabling superior characterization of stable individual neural signatures and dynamic task-dependent functional configurations. Furthermore, unlike PNC's hard-partitioned modularity, PEC captured highly overlapping yet functionally specialized modular structures and connector hubs, aligning with task-engaged cognitive processes. Applied to dyadic interactions, PEC identified distinct cross-brain modules encoding symmetric and asymmetric neural coordination. These findings establish PEC as a valid and powerful tool for EEG network modelling, providing new insights into the brain's complex, multifunctional organization at both intra-brain and inter-brain networks.
